gaps.sentence: The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (DETERMINE) to become a doctor never wavered.
gaps.explanation: A noun is needed after 'His': determination (-ation noun); 'determined' is the adjective.

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'His'; note the -al suffix
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'refuse' is 'refusal' (-al noun); 'refuse' as a noun means rubbish.

gaps.sentence: We need ___ proof before we can act (CONCLUDE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed before 'proof': conclusive (-ive). 'Conclusion' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: We had no ___ (CHOOSE) but to cancel the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Have no choice but to do something' is the fixed phrase; the noun of 'choose' is an irregular 'choice'.

gaps.sentence: Her suitcase was ___ , so the airline charged extra (WEIGHT).
gaps.hint: weighing too much — that is why she paid extra (over-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means too much: overweight explains the extra charge.

gaps.sentence: The team played ___ and deserved to win (EXCELLENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'played': excellently (-ly).
